newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Most HK people have faith in leader Tung -- poll.
newsitem.headline: Most HK people have faith in leader Tung -- poll.

text.p: More than three-quarters of Hong Kong people are optimistic that leader-in-waiting Tung Chee-hwa will do a good job when he takes office after the British colony's transfer to China, a poll showed on Wednesday.
The survey for the South China Morning Post newspaper found 75.2 percent of a sample of 586 people were confident Tung would perform well in the months after China resumes sovereignty on July 1.
Of the remainder, 16.1 percent said they were not confident and nine percent had no opinion, according to the poll, carried out by Asian Commercial Research on February 22-26.
The respondents were divided about whether colonial Governor Chris Patten had become irrelevant to Hong Kong since Tung was named as his post-colonial successor last December.

Some 48.8 percent did not think Patten, who has introduced democratic reforms which China plans to reverse, could achieve anything more during his final four months in office, while 46.6 percent believed he could.
Hong Kong is being returned to China under a 1984 treaty in which Beijing grants the territory a high degree of autonomy and lets it keep its capitalist system for a further 50 years.
